CHAPTER VIII
INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK
Article 16
(1) In the context of providing protection services to women and children from acts of violence, the Regional Government shall establish an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) or by another designation as an integrated service center in the protection of women and children from acts of violence including victims of acts of violence.

Article 20
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

b. Education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
c. Educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. Fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), are set forth in the form of an agreement.

CHAPTER III
CHILD-FRIENDLY REGENCY
Article 4
(1) In the framework of implementing the Convention on the Rights of the Child and various laws and regulations and policies related to the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children, the Regional Government, private sector and community institutions make efforts to realize a Child-Friendly Regency.
(2) To realize a Child-Friendly Regency as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government, private sector and Community Institutions pay attention to children's rights related to the right to life, growth and development, protection and participation.
(3) The Regional Government, Private Sector and Community Institutions in realizing a Child-Friendly Regency are incorporated in the Child-Friendly Regency Task Force.
(4) The Child-Friendly Regency Task Force is responsible for the fulfillment of children's rights related to:
a. Civil rights and freedoms;
b. Family environment and alternative care;
c. Basic health and welfare;
d. Education, use of leisure time and arts and cultural activities; e. Special protection of children.

CHILD-FRIENDLY REGENCY
Article 4
(1) In the framework of implementing the Convention on the Rights of the Child and various laws and regulations and policies related to the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children, the Regional Government, private sector and community institutions make efforts to realize a Child-Friendly Regency.
(2) To realize a Child-Friendly Regency as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government, private sector and Community Institutions pay attention to children's rights related to the right to life, growth and development, protection and participation.
(3) The Regional Government, Private Sector and Community Institutions in realizing a Child-Friendly Regency are incorporated in the Child-Friendly Regency Task Force.
(4) The Child-Friendly Regency Task Force is responsible for the fulfillment of children's rights related to:
a. Civil rights and freedoms;
b. Family environment and alternative care;
c. Basic health and welfare;
d. Education, use of leisure time and arts and cultural activities; e. Special protection of children.

CHAPTER XI
FINANCING
Article 23
Financing for the implementation of protection, Empowerment of women and children is sourced from:
a. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBN);
b. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD); and
c. Other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 24
(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that carry out protection, empowerment of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with the regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

CHAPTER X
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 21
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection, empowerment of women and children.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. Guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. Technical guidance and training;
c. Provision of facilities;
d. Monitoring; and
e. Evaluation.
(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2), is in order to realize the objectives of protection, empowerment of women and children in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by SKPD and the community.
(4) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted with the principles of professional, transparent, and accountable.

Article 22
